# Rules digest

Every error rule of `docs/rules/rules.toml` in one line; an agent brief includes this file
whole, with the topic's `NLAlib/<Topic>/RULES.md` (CONTRIBUTING §11). Warnings and review
rules are in the topic files; the reasons are in CONTRIBUTING.

- F1 Every file starts with the copyright header of the template.
- F2 A file is `module`, its imports, the module docstring, then `@[expose] public section`.
- F3 No `import Mathlib` or `import Mathlib.Tactic`.
- F4 A file outside ForMathlib puts its declarations in `namespace NLAlib`.
- F5 No file-level `set_option`.
- F6 Every `set_option maxHeartbeats N in` has a comment saying why.
- F7 No file-level `open Classical` or `open scoped Classical`.
- F8 No file-level `noncomputable section`.
- F9 No file-level `attribute [instance]`.
- P1 A module imports only its own layer and lower (§2 table); Krylov never imports Probability, Sketching never Regression, LowRank never Estimation.
- P2 No file with imports only (no per-directory aggregator).
- P3 An `NLAlib` file never imports `NLAlibScaffold`.
- P4 A ForMathlib statement uses no NLAlib vocabulary [ForMathlib only].
- P5 A ForMathlib declaration is in the Mathlib namespace it would have upstream, never `NLAlib` [ForMathlib only].
- P6 A ForMathlib module docstring marks the file as an upstream candidate [ForMathlib only].
- P8 Outside ForMathlib a declaration is in `NLAlib`, or is API of a Mathlib hypothesis structure.
- P9 A general fact (no NLAlib, matrix or measure vocabulary) lives in ForMathlib.
- P11 A Polynomial file imports only Mathlib, `NLAlib.ForMathlib` and `NLAlib.Polynomial` [Polynomial only].
- S1 No `simp_all`.
- S2 No search tactic left in (`exact?`, `apply?`, `rw?`, `simp?`, `aesop?`).
- S4 A proof has at most 80 lines.
- S6 No global instance on a Mathlib type, unless it is the one Mathlib would add.
- S7 A line has at most 100 characters, unless one identifier or a URL makes it long.
- S8 `set_option linter.style.longLine false in` only on a declaration with a long line.
- T1 The Euclidean norm is `‖WithLp.toLp 2 x‖`, never `√(x ⬝ᵥ x)`.
- T2 An `ℝ≥0` quantity in a statement is written with `‖·‖₊`, never `Real.toNNReal`.
- T3 Only `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` is opened, never `…Frobenius` or `…Elementwise`.
- T8 No statement quantifies over `eigenvectorBasis`.
- T9 No proof term inside a statement (`⋯` in the signature).
- T10 A bound variable that meets `•` has its type written (`∀ θ : ℝ, …`).
- T13 No hypothesis named `_h…`: an unused hypothesis is dropped.
- T15 A lower moment obtained by Jensen from a higher one is not a separate theorem.
- V1 Orthonormal columns are `HasOrthonormalCols Q`, never a raw `Qᴴ * Q = 1`.
- V2 No truncated subtraction `Fintype.card n - k` in a statement.
- V3 A singular-value ratio is `singularGapRatio`, never spelled out.
- V4 A squared Frobenius norm is `frobNorm A ^ 2`, never `frobNorm A * frobNorm A`.
- V5 No forbidden spelling (`matrixExp`, `matrixLog`, `traceExp`, `lambdaMax`, `conditionNumber`).
- V6 Every Lean name cited in CONTRIBUTING (outside §4) or Mathlib-deviations.md exists.
- B1 A named bound (`…Constant`, `…Bound`, `…Tail`, `…Dim`, `…Factor`) is in docs/constants.toml.
- B2 No bare `∃ C` in a statement, except in an `exists_forall_` asymptotic form.
- B3 An asymptotic form says "$O(\ldots)$ suffices" in its docstring.
- B4 An asymptotic form puts its constants first and fixes index types to `Type`.
- D1 A `Result:` declaration starts its docstring with a bold name.
- D2 A docstring states its own hypotheses and notation, never deferring to another statement.
- D4 No `\frac` in inline mathematics.
- D5 Punctuation after a `$$…$$` display goes inside it.
- D6 No Lean identifier inside `$…$`.
- D8 No `Proof:` sentence in a library docstring.
- D9 Every file has a module docstring.
- D10 A module docstring starts with `# Title` and has `## Main results`.
- D11 Every name a module docstring lists is declared.
- D12 A docstring says when summands are independent; a headline theorem names its laws.
- M1 A probability is `\mathbb{P}[E]`, never with round or brace delimiters, never `\Pr`.
- M2 A `Result:` theorem about an algorithm writes its output `\mathsf{name}(…)`.
- M4 `\mathsf{x}` is a declaration name or a short name registered in §5.3.
- M6 The Frobenius norm is `\|\mathbf{A}\|_{\mathsf{F}}`.
- M7 Adjoint and transpose are `^{\mathsf{H}}` and `^{\mathsf{T}}`.
- M8 `\varepsilon` and `\varphi`, never `\epsilon` or `\phi`.
- M9 Operator names follow the notation table (`\operatorname{tr}`, `\det`, …).
- M10 Expectation is `\mathbb{E}`.
- M11 A bold Greek matrix is `\mathbf{\Sigma}`.
- M12 Standard LaTeX only: no custom or KaTeX-only macro.
- M13 The `RCLike` field is `\Bbbk`.
- M14 The truncated SVD is `\llbracket\mathbf{A}\rrbracket_k`.
- M17 The Loewner order is `\preceq`.
- C1 A `Result:` declaration cites `[Key, label]` or says "No printed source.".
- C2 A declaration docstring cites with a label; a bare `[Key]` is for module docstrings only.
- C3 No mathematics inside a citation bracket.
- C4 Every citation-like bracket is one `check_refs.py` parses.
- C5 A bibliography key is `AuthorSurnames` + year.
- C6 No duplicate bibliography key or DOI.
- C7 The bibliography is alphabetical by key.
- R1 `Result:` ids go on statements, never on definitions or structures.
- R2 No two result ids one or two edits apart.
- R3 Every id or declaration the explorer names exists.
- G1 A Mathlib-deviations entry has Mathlib, NLAlib, Bridge, Why, Cost, Status.
- G2 Every port-ledger target is declared.
- E1 A program is generic in its handles and indices and takes no host data (`ℕ` sizes, lists, functions).
- E2 Programs, kernels and implementations are computable.
- E3 A realisation's program and initial state use no data of its interpretation (dimensions, tags and names excepted).
- E4 Every `<spec>Prog` has its realisation `runsWithin_<spec>Prog`.
- E5 A Computation file imports only Mathlib, `NLAlib.ForMathlib` and `NLAlib.Computation` [Computation only].
- E6 Only `NLAlib/Computation` defines a `ScalarSem` or an `Interp`.
- E8 `Stmt.named` is constructed only in the BLAS and implementation files.
- N1 Case by kind: theorems snake_case, data lowerCamelCase, Props and structures UpperCamelCase.
- N2 The first token is the head of the conclusion (or `exists_`, `forall_`, `ae_`, `nonneg`, `pos`).
- N3 The conclusion part ends at the first `_of_` and names the main relation.
- N4 Every library-function token in a name occurs in the statement.
- N5 One token per concept: the spellings of §4.3, never a synonym.
- N6 A power comes after its argument: `f_sq`, `f_pow`, `f_rpow`.
- N7 No source, author, project, quality or role word in a name (`_sharp`, `aux`, `main`).
- N9 A law hypothesis is `_of_hasLaw_<law>`; an interface hypothesis is the namespace.
- N10 Errors are `exact − computed`: `norm_sub_<alg>`, never `<alg>_sub_`.
- N11 A named bound ends in its kind: `…Constant`, `…Factor`, `…Tail`, `…Bound`, `…Ratio`, `…Dim`.
- N13 A statistic on the left is the prefix: `integral_`, `variance_`; a mean square has `_sq`.
- N14 A tail is `measureReal_` for `μ.real {…}`, `measure_` for `μ {…}`.
- N15 A tail event is named subject first, with two relation tokens; stated positively.
- N16 A sample size is a named bound `<sketch><property>Dim` [LowRank, Regression, Sketching only].
- N17 An asymptotic form is `exists_forall_` + its explicit theorem's name, in the root namespace.
- N18 A theorem whose first explicit argument is `hA : A.P` lives in namespace `P` (dot notation).
